insights: Although motor vehicles are generally faster, some cycling trajectories outperform slower car trajectories during peak periods.
The speed advantage of motor vehicles becomes larger with the distance to the downtown area
Motor vehicle trajectories show larger speed variation than bikes with respect to trajectory progress generally
summary: Motor-vehicle trajectories are generally faster, but slow peak-period motor trips overlap with some cycling speeds. The motor-vehicle speed advantage grows farther from downtown, while motor-vehicle point speeds vary more within a trip than cycling point speeds.
evidence_policy: Claims describe patterns in this dataset and do not establish causal relationships.
